criteria.description: Correctly identifies plain Newton's local model has no constraint-handling mechanism.
Correctly explains SQP linearizes constraints and solves a constrained QP subproblem at each step.

solutions.fullSolution: Newton's local model minimizes a quadratic approximation of f over an unconstrained step delta. Plain Newton has no way to keep x+delta feasible: nothing in its model references g or h. SQP keeps the same quadratic objective model but additionally linearizes the constraints (g(x)+grad g^T delta <= 0, h(x)+grad h^T delta = 0) and solves the resulting constrained QP subproblem at each iteration, giving a step that respects the constraints locally.

criteria.description: Correctly identifies the dropped curvature-of-residuals term.
Correctly explains when it's large and when full Newton is preferable.

solutions.fullSolution: Exact Hessian = 2J^T J + 2 sum_i phi_i(x) grad^2 phi_i(x); Gauss-Newton drops the second term. It's large when residuals phi_i(x) are large or highly curved -- far from a good fit. If the exact Hessian is affordable and residuals are large, full Newton captures this term and can converge better; Gauss-Newton's advantage (cheap, always PSD) is most worth keeping specifically in the small-residual regime.

criteria.description: Correctly identifies the constraint is active and sets up stationarity.
Correctly solves for x*=(1,1), lambda*=2, f(x*)=2.

solutions.fullSolution: g(x)=2-x1-x2<=0; unconstrained min (0,0) is infeasible, so g(x*)=0. Stationarity: (2x1,2x2)+lambda(-1,-1)=0 => x1=x2=lambda/2. With x1+x2=2: lambda=2, x1=x2=1. f(x*)=2. lambda=2>=0 confirms dual feasibility. Independently verified via grid search along the constraint boundary.

criteria.description: Correctly sets up stationarity with the new constraint gradient.
Correctly solves for x*=(0.6,1.2), lambda*=1.2, f(x*)=1.8.

solutions.fullSolution: g(x)=3-x1-2x2<=0, active at optimum. Stationarity: (2x1,2x2)+lambda(-1,-2)=0 => x1=lambda/2, x2=lambda. With x1+2x2=3: lambda/2+2lambda=3 => lambda=1.2. x*=(0.6,1.2), f(x*)=1.8. Independently verified via grid search.

criteria.description: Correctly derives the general stationarity condition combining OPT-02's gradient formula with the Lagrangian.
Correctly solves the concrete case: x*=(1.5,2.5), kappa*=-1, f(x*)=0.5.

solutions.fullSolution: L(x,kappa)=phi(x)^T phi(x)+kappa h(x). Stationarity: 2J(x)^T phi(x)+kappa grad h(x)=0, plus h(x)=0. For phi=(x1-1,x2-2), J=I: 2(x1-1,x2-2)+kappa(1,1)=0 => x1=1-kappa/2, x2=2-kappa/2. With h=x1+x2-4=0: 3-kappa=4 => kappa=-1, x*=(1.5,2.5), f(x*)=0.5. Independently verified via grid search.

criteria.description: Correctly sets up stationarity for the new phi/h.

solutions.fullSolution: J=I again. 2(x1-3,x2+1)+kappa(1,-1)=0 => x1=3-kappa/2, x2=-1+kappa/2. With h=x1-x2-5=0: 4-kappa=5 => kappa=-1, x*=(3.5,-1.5), f(x*)=0.5. Independently verified via grid search.
